headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 7 studies yielded an effect size of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.51–1.08), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin D and aggressive prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 81.92%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
